text: Article 14 of the Constitution of India guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. In FairPay, this is a constitutional principle relevant to equal treatment and non-discriminatory treatment of workers.

Article 15 of the Constitution of India prohibits discrimination by the State on specified grounds including religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. In FairPay, it provides constitutional context for discrimination-related findings.
Article 19(1)(g) of the Constitution of India protects the right of citizens to practise any profession or to carry on any occupation, trade or business, subject to constitutional restrictions.
Article 21 of the Constitution of India protects life and personal liberty according to procedure established by law. It provides constitutional context for dignity and personal liberty.
Article 23 of the Constitution of India prohibits trafficking in human beings and forced labour.

Article 39(d) of the Constitution of India directs the State to secure equal pay for equal work for both men and women. This is a Directive Principle and should not be treated by FairPay as a standalone payment rule for every gig worker.

Article 39(e) of the Constitution of India directs the State to ensure that the health and strength of workers are not abused and that citizens are not forced by economic necessity into unsuitable work.

Article 41 of the Constitution of India directs the State, within its economic capacity and development, to make effective provision for the right to work, education and public assistance in certain cases.
Article 42 of the Constitution of India directs the State to make provision for securing just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.

Article 43 of the Constitution of India directs the State to secure work, a living wage, conditions of work ensuring a decent standard of life and full enjoyment of leisure and social and cultural opportunities for workers.
The Code on Wages, 2019 contains a prohibition on discrimination on the ground of gender in matters relating to wages by the employer in respect of the same work or work of a similar nature.

Section 5 of the Code on Wages, 2019 provides that no employer shall pay to any employee wages less than the minimum rate of wages notified by the appropriate Government, subject to the applicability of the Code.
Section 13 of the Code on Wages, 2019 concerns fixing the number of hours that constitute a normal working day and provides for rest intervals as prescribed.
Section 14 of the Code on Wages, 2019 provides for wages for overtime work at a rate which shall not be less than twice the normal rate of wages, subject to the applicable framework.
Section 18 of the Code on Wages, 2019 provides that deductions from wages are permitted only when authorised under the Code.
Section 113 of the Code on Social Security, 2020 concerns registration of unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers for the purposes of the relevant social security provisions.

Section 114 of the Code on Social Security, 2020 provides for schemes for gig workers and platform workers covering matters such as life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity benefits, old age protection, crèche and other benefits. It also provides for aggregator contributions subject to the statutory framework and notifications.
Section 7 of the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 provides rights of platform based gig workers under the Act.

text: Section 12 of the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 requires fair contracts between aggregators or platforms and platform based gig workers.
statute: Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025

text: Section 13 of the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 concerns transparency in automated monitoring and decision making systems. Platforms must provide information about relevant automated decision parameters affecting working conditions, including fares and earnings, and must take measures to prevent specified forms of discrimination.
statute: Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025

text: Section 14 of the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 regulates termination of work. Contracts must contain grounds for termination or deactivation. Generally, termination or deactivation requires valid written reasons, fourteen days prior notice and observance of principles of natural justice, subject to the statutory exception for certain bodily-harm situations.
statute: Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025

text: Section 15 of the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 concerns income security. Where payments are deducted, the aggregator or platform must inform the gig worker of the reasons for deductions in the invoice. Payouts must follow the contract and the statutory payout-cycle requirements.
statute: Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025

text: Section 16 of the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 concerns reasonable working conditions. Platforms must, as far as reasonably practicable, provide a working environment that is safe and without risk to the health of the platform based gig worker, including adequate rest periods and access to sanitary and rest facilities.
statute: Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025

text: Section 17 of the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 requires disclosure of information concerning grievance redressal and dispute resolution mechanisms.
statute: Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025

text: Section 20 of the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 establishes a welfare fee payable by aggregators or platforms within the statutory framework. The Act provides for a welfare fee of not less than one percent and not more than five percent of the relevant payout base specified by the Act.
statute: Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025

text: Section 21 of the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 concerns the Payment and Welfare Fee Verification System. Transaction-level payment and welfare-fee information is to be recorded and reported according to the Act and Rules.
statute: Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025

text: Section 22 of the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 provides grievance redressal mechanisms for registered platform based gig workers, including grievances concerning payouts, deductions and termination.
statute: Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025

text: Section 24 of the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025 concerns submission of quarterly returns by aggregators or platforms.
statute: Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025

text: Rule 10 of the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Rules, 2025 concerns the mechanism through which platform based gig workers can seek information regarding fares, earnings and customer feedback that may affect their work.
statute: Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Rules, 2025

text: Rule 20 of the Karnataka Platform Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Rules, 2025 provides for recording payments made to platform based gig workers and welfare-fee deductions in the Payment and Welfare Fee Verification System in machine-readable form within the prescribed period.
